findings.title: BMI
findings.text: Median BMI is 27 in class 0 and 31 in class 1. The distributions overlap, so the difference supports an association without giving a reliable single-value classification rule.

findings.title: High blood pressure
findings.text: Class 1 accounts for 6.03% of respondents without high blood pressure and 24.46% of those with it. The difference makes this a useful candidate predictor, but it may also reflect age or other shared characteristics.

findings.title: General health
findings.text: The class-1 proportion is 2.52% for excellent health and 38.06% for poor health. These self-reported categories relate strongly to the target. The data do not establish whether poor health precedes the condition or reflects its consequences.

findings.title: Age
findings.text: The class-1 proportion is 1.42% at ages 18-24. It peaks at 22.03% in the 70-74 group, compared with 18.38% at 80+. Read the actual category pattern rather than assuming that each older group must have a higher proportion. Age is a grouped predictor, not an exact age.

findings.title: Heavy alcohol indicator
findings.text: Class-1 proportions are 14.41% for code 0 and 5.81% for code 1. This observed association cannot establish a protective effect: group composition, reporting differences, or behaviour following diagnosis could contribute.
